provenance.contractDescription: Machine-readable scoring/methodology contract. Validated at the start of every benchmark run. Changing this file is a methodology change and requires a version bump (see FAIRNESS-V1-PLAN.md, B8/26). v1.1 added the safety-probe schema 2.0 guarantees (B5/B6). v1.2 added safety tracks including RESOURCE_FAILURE and the minimum probe repeat count (B9/B10/B11). v1.3 added knowledge-track labels and the equal documentation budget (B19). v1.4 added labeled generation-budget levels. v1.5 adds the prompt interface contract (the harness API is given to every LLM). v1.6 adds the per-language correctness oracles: task-specific t4-packet and t5-btree harnesses with the checksum/pseudo-header and b-tree semantics pinned to the C reference, the arena template syncs those need, and the t3-hot-reload fixture architecture (built testdata modules, module_arity fixture ABI, unload return code). v1.7 completes the t3-hot-reload per-language oracles (C++ class loader API, Rust extern C dlopen, Zig std.DynLib, Go cgo, Ada Module_Loader spec, XIOM Vec-backed loader with extern C wrappers) and aligns every t3 template with the harness contract; the C oracle semantics stay pinned. v1.8 pins arena/reference compile-flag parity for XIOM (performance binaries build with the config.yaml flag set; the t8/t9 safety probe keeps --no-contracts --overflow-checks as documented in the t8 spec) per the B25 benchmark-special audit (docs/BENCHMARK-SPECIAL-AUDIT.md). v1.9 is the non-XIOM fairness repair: every compiled language gets an accurate entry-point instruction (Go was missing; Ada is told the truth that its fixed package interface is composed by the benchmark), the t1/t2/t5 Zig templates drop unsupported block comments, and the t3 contract-variant templates (c-contracts, cpp-contracts, rust-prusti, ada-spark) now expose the same interface as their plain siblings with honest annotation/verification bases (no formal verifier is installed for Prusti/SPARK in this image; see docs/FAIRNESS-OPTIONS-2026-09-26.md). v1.10 retires the t3-hot-reload extern-C dlopen/dlsym/dlclose workaround: the image now carries XIOM 0.62.1 (R-5 fixed), so all five t3 templates and the conformance solution use the stdlib xiom.ffi.dl module; the task set is re-frozen after that template change. v1.11 adds the missing XIOM template for t6-script-correctness (base task plus the scripting-llm/scripting-arena task dirs): the xiom-run family now receives the same harness-interface section as the sibling scripting languages (prompt symmetry), and the Test Inspector lists all 8 scripting languages for the task. The task set is re-frozen for that template addition; no scoring rule changed. v1.12 replaces the simulated t3-hot-reload references with real dynamic-module-loading implementations in every arena (dlopen/dlsym/dlclose via libc in C/C++/Rust/Go/Ada, std.DynLib in Zig, xiom.ffi.dl in XIOM; identical 1000-cycle x 100-call workload over libc.so.6/abs with a deterministic checksum) and links libc in the Zig arena build (-lc) so Zig performs the same real dynamic loading as every other systems language; the correctness harness already linked libc for the same reason. config.yaml changed; no task or scoring change. v1.13 enables the correctness phase in the scripting arena now that its references are real: scripting subjects receive JSON-op input (not the compiled harness's flattened lines that made every parse fail), suite fixtures (t7 test.bin) are materialized in the run directory, and the t7 suite expectations were repaired to be honest (empty JSON input is an error case -- no_crash; HTTP reachability is not a language property -- the request is performed, no_crash asserted, URL pinned to 127.0.0.1). Lua runs and is probed as 5.4 (the image default `lua` is 5.1) and the image ships lua-socket for its 5.4 build; the Lua t6 reference's missing forward declarations (nil global crash on every parse) are fixed. The task set is re-frozen for the t7 suite and Lua reference changes; no scoring rule changed. v1.14 makes the LLM arenas measure the MODEL, not language speed: the two-run-mode XIOM entries (xiom-run, xiom-run-aot/jit/cache) leave the LLM profiles and are replaced by the knowledge tracks (systems/contracts-llm use xiom-zero/xiom-rag/xiom-mcp; scripting-llm uses the new xiom-run-zero/rag/mcp entries), and every LLM trial now records generation/think time (wall-clock generation, compile/test execution excluded) alongside tokens and iterations. The Scripting Arena keeps the run modes (that is where language speed belongs). config.yaml changed; no task or scoring change. v1.15 bumps the tested XIOM toolchain to v0.62.2 (Gate P / PERF-1 acceptance): the image installs the v0.62.2 release with SHA256 verification and the systems arena is re-run over t2-queue plus t1/t3/t4/t5/t8 for regression evidence. No task or scoring change. v1.16 removes every extra scripting execution mode (owner rule, restated 2026-10-01): XIOM scripting runs in a SINGLE mode (JIT) for both the Scripting Arena and the LLM knowledge tracks, so `xiom-run-aot`/`xiom-run-jit`/`xiom-run-cache` are deleted, labels never name the mode (XIOM / XIOM (zero-shot) / XIOM + RAG / XIOM + MCP + AI), the dead runtime-mode filter and Settings panel are gone, and `tracks.xiom_run_modes` records the single mode jit. config.yaml changed; no task or scoring change. v1.17 restores the four XIOM scripting execution modes in the Scripting Arena only (owner item 4): xiom-run (JIT+cache baseline), xiom-run-jit (cold JIT, explicit --no-cache), xiom-run-aot (AOT, explicit --no-cache) and xiom-run-cache (AOT+cache, reference-only). --no-cache is explicit because the v0.62.2 binary cache defaults ON, so a mode that claims to be cache-free must disable it; the cached AOT mode is displayed with a disclosure but excluded from every composite, ranking and comparison (owner item 5, fairness: cached repeated-source runs are not a language measurement), and LLM profiles keep exactly the three knowledge tracks. config.yaml changed; no task or scoring change. v1.18 records the LLM-arena behavior updates: per-track AI policy (zero-shot receives NO AI assist -- no xiom --ai, no MCP tools, compile feedback only; RAG uses direct xiom --ai diagnostics with the diagnostic provider's model and an explicit 60s AI timeout; MCP uses real MCP tool calls -- explain_error_code plus ai_diagnose when a provider is configured -- recorded per trial), LLM trial budgets raised to fit max_iterations x generation deadline (300s -> 1200s for systems-llm/contracts-llm/scripting-llm), safety/safety-sanitized recorded as explicit skips on non-t8/t9 tasks instead of parse-failure phases, and the injected knowledge context included in the no-usage token estimate (prompt account already included it). Proof bundles are an export/verification tool and do not change scoring. No task or scoring change. v1.19 pins the tested XIOM toolchain to v0.62.3 (official SHA256-verified release archive, Linux asset 4cc5d62b...): PERF-1 is accepted -- t2-queue drops from 11,968 ms (v0.62.2) to 24 ms with no regression on t1/t3/t4/t5/t8 and identical t8 safety indices; the benchmark lane validated the tag locally before publish (candidate archive 518f123f...) and re-checks the official archive. v1.19 also fixes two fairness/data defects found in review: composite metric scores are now normalized per task across every scored language (or per contract tier when tiered) so a language alone in its execution-mode group can no longer score a perfect 100 by having no peer, and the per-trial safety LSI is persisted on the trial row (schema V13) instead of being dropped, so the Safety Profile/Analyze surfaces show ada/go and every other language. Trial ids now embed the arena slug (`..._system_`, `..._contracts_`, `..._scripting_`) and never an LLM model on non-LLM arenas. No task change; task_set_hash unchanged. v1.20 re-freezes the task set for the t8 safety documentation/scoring alignment: the spec and config scoring_method now describe the 12-probe registry, the scored-probe-normalized LSI (floor(sum/(scored*10)*100), INCONCLUSIVE excluded), the schema-1.0 vs schema-2.0 comparability rule (legacy evidence is never ranked against observed canary/sentinel evidence) and the honest t9 label ("ASan/UBSan" only where a sanitizer build ran, else "recheck (no sanitizer)"). The v1.19 epoch hash e9c838eb... and its sessions remain valid as their own epoch; no scoring rule changed. v1.21 (P1.1/P1.2, hardening plan) migrates the C t8 safety fixture to schema 2.0: all 12 probes run fork-isolated with volatile canary/sentinel guards, the probe child carries observed evidence to the parent over a pipe, and the parent classifies from that evidence (INCONCLUSIVE stays unscored). The t8 spec now states C and XIOM are observed while C++/Rust/Zig/Go/Ada remain legacy-normalized until their own per-language re-freeze. P1.2 adds the failure-class attribution vocabulary (LANGUAGE_RULE/COMPILER_ENFORCEMENT/RUNTIME/UNSAFE_BOUNDARY/FFI/HARNESS/UNKNOWN): silent safe-subset outcomes attribute to COMPILER_ENFORCEMENT, containment silences to RUNTIME, documented-unsafe silences to UNSAFE_BOUNDARY, and unobserved probes to HARNESS. P1.3 adds the optional held-out tree hash to the manifest when tasks/held_out is supplied. No scoring rule changed. v1.22 migrates the C++ t8 fixture to the same schema-2.0 design (new/delete, reinterpret_cast; observed canary/sentinel evidence) and finalizes the P1.3 held-out selection wiring (`ho-` tasks resolve from tasks/held_out through run overrides and the orchestrator; the public-tree leak gate is unchanged). P1.4 adds the differential validity disclosure (cross-language correctness disagreements are listed in the report model and markdown; affected performance cells are marked unvalidated). No scoring rule changed. v1.23 migrates the Rust t8 fixture to schema 2.0 observed evidence (12 fork-isolated probes, volatile canary/sentinel guards, pipe-carried observations, parent classification; stdout built in memory and flushed before every fork so child buffers cannot corrupt the JSON). v1.24 migrates the Zig t8 fixture to schema 2.0 observed evidence (12 fork-isolated probes via linux.fork/pipe2, volatile canary/sentinel guards, pipe-carried observations, parent classification; libc malloc/free used directly so the Zig probe observes the same allocator behavior as C, and the whole JSON is built in memory and printed once after every fork). v1.25 migrates the Go t8 fixture to schema 2.0 observed evidence (12 probes, each isolated in a re-executed child because fork is not usable from the Go runtime; canary/sentinel observed through sync/atomic; the child carries the observation over stdout and the parent classifies from it; double-free and invalid-free are attempted through cgo C.malloc/C.free -- no manual free exists in pure Go -- so they reach the same glibc allocator as the C/C++/Zig fixtures, documented in the probe). v1.26 completes the P1.1 migration: the Ada t8 fixture is schema 2.0 observed evidence (12 probes in forked children through POSIX fork/pipe imports -- the same libc the C fixture uses -- with a Volatile guard type, pipe-carried observations and parent classification; the checks-enabled GNAT build raises Constraint_Error/Storage_Error/Program_Error for the detected operations, the observed survivors are canary-checked, and no legacy score-only fixture remains in the task set). v1.27 adds warm-up capture: each arena speed/throughput/startup test keeps the cold first run's wall time as a separate warmup_ms metric (persisted per trial via schema V15 and surfaced in the raw report, report model, evidence index and Analyze view) instead of discarding it; the dashboard safety panel self-heals when the probe matrix lands after the run; and loaded LLM sessions state their language/runtime versions (incl. the XIOM compiler) next to the thought-process context. v1.28 installs the two formal verifiers the contracts arena probes: gnatprove (SPARK FSF 15.1.0, pinned upstream tarball hash) and Prusti (v-2023-08-22 with its pinned nightly-2023-08-15 toolchain and JRE). Both run only inside their subsets -- gnatprove when a source opts into SPARK (the Ada/SPARK reference is outside the SPARK subset, so its legality result is disclosed and the trial falls back to -gnata runtime checks) and Prusti only on real Prusti attribute specs (the current Rust/Prusti reference carries none) -- so no spec-less file can receive a fabricated formal pass. v1.29 fixes the DeepSeek lane end to end: the hand-written keep-alive headers that made every call fail with an undici invalid-header transport error are gone, provider model/endpoint selections persist across restarts, declared reasoning models default to the max completion budget (32768) unless an explicit level is chosen, and the code-only retry escalates the budget; the dashboard language tabs (Live Code, compiler terminal, thought process, comparison grid) now show only the candidates selected for the run, and the Settings model list reports fetch errors and the provider's real model ids. No scoring rule changed. v1.30 follows the owner's live-run report: the per-generation deadline now scales with the resolved budget (minimum 300s, ~20ms/token, 656s at the max reasoning budget) instead of aborting every 32768-token generation at a flat 300s, and the LLM thought panel distinguishes a pending language (waiting for the first response) from a genuinely failed one (provider failed before a response) instead of claiming failure for trials that are still generating. No scoring rule changed. v1.31 fixes long-generation transport after a live 4-language report: OpenAI-compatible providers now stream (stream: true with stream_options.include_usage; a non-streaming request is terminated by the DeepSeek gateway after ~60s of silence, reproduced in-container, so content/reasoning are accumulated from deltas and usage comes from the final chunk with an explicit estimate when absent). Additionally the configured generation_deadline_seconds is now a FLOOR: each attempt gets max(floor, ~20ms per token of its budget) and the code-only retry re-arms its own larger deadline (LLM trial budgets 1200s -> 3600s). No scoring rule changed. v1.32 pins the tested XIOM toolchain to the official v0.64.1 archive (contracts-lane m213 locals sort lookup + havoc loop summary, JIT script-cache m208, Pulse/XVECTOR codegen fixes) and raises the Scripting Arena per-trial timeout from 300s to 900s: the cold JIT/AOT modes recompile every sample and a t7 trial exceeded the old cap under load (a passing trial still logged the timeout warning). Retest on the pinned image: contracts t1 improves to 2 proven / 0 violated / 10 unknown / 0 errors with no false violations; t4/t5/t8 still emit no queries, so reference annotations remain blocked; lz4 3/3, t2 7/7 with XIOM at 28ms, scripting XIOM modes 8/8, t8 safety LSI 30. No scoring rule changed. v1.33 closes the contracts reference gap the compiler lane isolated (clause-free references give the verifier zero obligations): the XIOM t2/t3/t4/t5 references now carry at least one provable obligation each -- single-sourced constants with an equality postcondition (t3 reload_cycles, t5 node_capacity, plus t2 default_capacity and t4 header_len) and preconditions on t2 SPSCQueue.new and t4 parse_packet/compute_checksum. Retest on v0.64.1: t2 1 proven/0 violated/2 unknown, t3 1/0/0, t4 1/0/4, t5 1/0/0 -- all PROVEN and the contracts trials pass 4/4 (t3 Linux speed median 213ms, unchanged). t8 stays unproven (raw memory the SMT encoder cannot model; the next archive's m233 reduces its unknowns to 1). Known gap: reference/ is not covered by the manifest task hashes. No scoring rule changed. v1.34 makes every arena's safety evidence schema 2.0 and closes the last contracts FAIL: the systems-contracts-arena t8-safety-probe fixtures for C, C++, Rust, Zig, Go and Ada were still the legacy 8-probe copies (only XIOM had been migrated), so the contracts Safety Profile showed legacy evidence and the arena catalogs disagreed; all copies are now byte-identical to the systems-arena schema-2.0 fixtures (contracts t8 run: 6/6, every language 12 observed, 3 repeats). The t8 XIOM reference also gains a provable obligation (probe_count() with ensures result == N_PROBES, used as the main loop bound) so its contracts trial records 1 proven / 0 violated / 3 unknown / 0 errors instead of an unproven zero-proven-obligation failure. No scoring rule changed.

safety.note: Primary view is the Safety Profile (per-track rates + probe matrix); LSI is derived and shown below the raw probes. LSI values are only directly comparable between languages with the same evidence schema (probe_comparability/probe_schema): observed canary-backed probes are schema 2.0, legacy score-only probes are normalized as 1.0 and disclosed, never upgraded.
